kf: Most neonatal rashes are **benign and transient**: erythema toxicum neonatorum (ETN), transient neonatal pustular melanosis (TNPM), miliaria, milia and neonatal acne.
ETN: blotchy red macules with central pustules in days 1–3; spares palms and soles; eosinophils.
TNPM: pustules at birth that rupture to leave collarettes and brown macules, more in darker skin.
Miliaria: blocked sweat ducts from overheating; clear vesicles (crystallina) or red papules (rubra).
Red flags: unwell baby, vesicles (**HSV**: emergency aciclovir), purpura, blistering, widespread pustules with fever.

sub: ETN affects up to half of term babies; TNPM about 5% of Black infants; miliaria in hot, overwrapped babies.

myths: **"Spots in a newborn mean infection"**: most are harmless, but vesicles or an unwell baby need urgent review.
patho_lead: Newborn skin is **adapting** to air, bacteria and temperature regulation.

mech.t: ETN reflects an innate immune response to colonising bacteria at hair follicles (eosinophils).
Immature ducts block easily, causing miliaria when overheated.
mech.cap: Milia: tiny keratin cysts common on newborn noses and cheeks.

mech.t: Maternal androgens stimulate sebaceous glands (neonatal acne, sebaceous hyperplasia).

sub: Grouped vesicles, especially on the scalp or presenting part, with or without fever: emergency IV aciclovir.

comp: Rarely, misdiagnosis of infection; miliaria pustulosa can become infected.
prog: ETN and TNPM resolve within days to weeks (TNPM pigment within months).
